KEY MESSAGE 1: Strong low pressure system will bring widespread rainfall and
gusty winds to the area on Thanksgiving Day.


Heading into tomorrow, a complex upper level pattern will lead 
to unsettled weather through the Thanksgiving holiday across the
region. Two upper level shortwave features, with one across the
Gulf states, and another across the central Conus look to aid 
in the development of a rather strong surface low off the coast 
of Florida on Wednesday. The upper level shortwave across the 
Gulf looks to become negatively tilted as it enters the northern
Gulf, and will provide significant upper level forcing for 
ascent and divergence aloft along the baroclinic zone off the 
east coast of the US. This will quickly deepen the surface low 
as it tracks north along the coast of the Carolinas. As this 
occurs, the second upper level shortwave trough looks to enter 
the middle Mississippi valley by Thursday morning, and is also 
expected to become negatively tilted by this point. Not only 
will this continue to aid in deepening the surface low, which 
should be over eastern North Carolina, but it will also 
possibly pull the surface low slightly to the northwest as it 
deepens and tracks northward with time. This is where models 
differ ever so slightly as the ECMWF model wants to bring the 
surface low more along the leading edge of the aforementioned 
wedge front across eastern North Carolina and SE Virginia, but 
the GFS has been consistent on bringing this low slightly more 
inland towards central North Carolina and Virginia.

Timing differences among both models has seemed to come into
better agreement this model cycle. Regardless, this low 
pressure system will likely impact the region with strong winds 
and heavy rainfall starting late Wednesday night and all day 
Thursday. 

An east/southeast 60-70 knot LLJ at 850mb looks to develop with
this deepening surface low. These winds will likely mix down to
the surface beyond the surface wedge/inversion layer Wednesday
night into Thursday morning. These winds look to be near or just
below Advisory levels at the surface, with widespread 30 to 40 
mph wind gusts likely. Portions of NW North Carolina and SW 
Virginia have been put under a Wind Advisory for the time being 
as these areas will likely experience these strong winds prior 
to the rest of the area. Future expansions of this Wind Advisory
will be possible given this intense LLJ moving into the area. 

Along with the wind, precipitation totals look impressive with 
this system, with expected rainfall totals in the 1.0 to 2.0
inch range are expected for much of the forecast area. Areas
west of the Blue Ridge will likely be closer to the 1.0 inch
range, with SE West Virginia and western facing slopes of SW
Virginia likely seeing 0.50 to 1.0 inches of rainfall due to
downsloping impacts. 

For areas along and east of the Blue Ridge, there is a 75 to 85%
chance of seeing greater than 1.5 inches of rainfall. Certain
areas right along the Blue Ridge may see enhanced rainfall
totals due to upsloping influences from the aforementioned LLJ.
Overall, the rainfall totals forecast from this system will be
beneficial to the area; however, there is a small chance for 
nuisance flooding with this system from recently fallen leaves 
clogging drainage flows, the overall threat for flooding remains
somewhat low given the ongoing drought concerns and weeks with 
little to no rainfall across the region. 

By Thursday night, the low is expected to lift north of the
region, and winds will transition to westerly/northwesterly
across the area as the aforementioned upper level shortwave 
trough pushes east over the region. This will will lead to some
upslope rain/snow showers across SE West Virginia and SW 
Virginia Thursday night into Friday. Light snowfall
accumulations look possible in western Greenbrier Friday night.
As winds transition, an 850mb northwesterly LLJ in the 40-50 
knot range looks to develop over the region, which will likely 
mix down to the surface leading to a gusty shopping day for many
on Friday. 

Calmer weather looks to return for the weekend as high pressure
settles south of the region through Sunday.
